{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABcrmNJQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhGNufI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 134, "title": "Implement the related missing PC-98 INT 18h CRT/KCG text-mode, display-area and cursor BIOS services together", "body": "## Problem

After installing and launching a locally held PC-98 DOS game in the freshly booted FreeDOS(98) desktop, the emulator stops with:

```
unsupported BIOS INT 18 AH=1b
```

The prior high-conventional-memory issue is resolved ([Issue #132 / PR #133](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/133)), so this is a **distinct missing PC-98 BIOS compatibility feature**, not an HDD size or DOS configuration issue.

**Do not implement only `AH=1Bh` and stop at the next unsupported call.** Implement the small, related CRT/text-display, character-generator-access and cursor BIOS family together, using one coherent state model, accurate contracts and shared tests.

### Important specification correction

Some interrupt catalogs summarize `INT 18h / AH=1Bh` as “set display mode,” but the original NEC documentation identifies it **specifically as setting KCG (Kanji character generator) access mode**:

- `AH=1Bh`, `AL=00h`: **code access**; `AL=01h`: **dot/bitmap access**. Mode influences font/CG access and Kanji handling, **not an arbitrary graphics-resolution switch**.
- Related unimplemented `AH=1Ch`: **initialize CRT** (including KCG access and cursor configuration); `AH=1Dh`: **set display width / GDC columns**; `AH=1Eh`: **set cursor shape/blink**.
- The related `AH=0Fh` **multiple text display-area** command is also missing, while adjacent `AH=0Eh` (one display area) is partially implemented.
- Existing `AH=0Ah/0Bh` text-mode set/sense, `AH=10h–13h` cursor/display services and `AH=14h/1Ah` font/user-character handling must be consistent with these changes. They currently have simplified behavior.

**Authoritative contract**: *PC-9800 Series Technical Data Book, BIOS volume* (1992), Chapter 3, **printed pp. 41–59**, especially pp. **43–46 and 53–55**:
- https://vtda.org/docs/computing/NEC/PC-9800TechnicalDataBookBIOS%2BOCR_1992.pdf
- https://pc98.ne.jp/devdocs/pc-9800technicaldatabookbios.pdf
Additional independent prose description of `AH=1Bh`: https://vtda.org/books/Computing/Programming/PC-9801Bible_%E6%9D%B1%E4%BA%AC%E7%90%86%E7%A7%91%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6.pdf

Do not copy, translate, port or consult another emulator's **implementation code** as an implementation shortcut. Use hardware/BIOS specifications, original Rust code and original guest probes.

## Expected outcome

On the **PC-9821Ap DOS** profile, legal DOS software can invoke the following coherent set without unsupported-BIOS traps, with meaningful guest-observable hardware behavior rather than no-op stubs:

**New implementations (one combined work item):**

1. **`INT 18h / AH=1Bh` — KCG access mode.** Correct AL parameter and profile handling; code vs dot access changes the already modeled CG access window and compatible text/Kanji rendering constraints. Coordinate BIOS entry with the existing port `68h` commands `0Ah/0Bh`, `Bus.cg_dot`, CG character registers `A1h/A3h/A5h`, font reads and user-defined character storage. Reflect any documented BIOS work-area state if applicable.
2. **`AH=1Ch` — CRT initialization.** Initialize documented text-mode, KCG access, cursor presence/shape and blink control from the supplied AL/DH/DL fields. Preserve specified register effects and do not reset unrelated graphics/VRAM/device state without documentary basis.
3. **`AH=1Dh` — display width.** Implement documented GDC column/pitch behavior and its interactions with text VRAM traversal, wrapping and on-screen rendering for supported Ap modes; do not merely accept a parameter without changing actual display behavior.
4. **`AH=1Eh` — cursor blink/shape control.** Implement documented input fields and correct cursor visibility/shape/blink handling, including interaction with existing `AH=10h–13h` commands, GDC cursor state and renderer timing.
5. **`AH=0Fh` — multiple text display areas.** Implement the documented, bounded text-display-area sequencing/state with real GDC integration, shared with existing `AH=0Eh`. Where scanout/timing needed for this is unsupported, add a minimal, genuine original-Rust implementation sufficient to observe correct area selection; don't fake multi-area execution with unconditional success.

**Coherent surrounding behavior:** Audit/fix `AH=0Ah/0Bh`, `0Ch–0Eh`, `10h–14h` and `1Ah` **only as necessary** to make that group consistent: set/sense round trips, mode bytes, code/dot accessibility, font/user-defined glyph visibility, text dimensions and cursor state. The current `AH=0Ah` simply writes BWA `053Ch` without changing text renderer modes, so this is not purely adding new `match` arms. Avoid wholesale redesign of graphics BIOS, full 24-dot/high-res font support, Windows, sound BIOS or all INT 18h subfunctions.

Document distinctions among PC-9801VM and PC-9821Ap. Implement **documented common 9801 functions on VM where appropriate**, but do not invent Ap-only KCG dot modes, 9821 features or unsupported high-resolution hardware for VM. If a particular submode is genuinely unsupported, preserve an accurate bounded error rather than silently accepting it. The reported `AH=1Bh` Ap path and all supported parameter modes are mandatory.

## Reproduction

1. In the browser desktop, fresh Ap boots FreeDOS(98) to `A:\>` using the bundled writable 128 MiB HDD.
2. A legally held game installer uses a user-supplied D88 in Floppy 1 and installs to the HDD. Running the game reaches `unsupported BIOS INT 18 AH=1b`. **The private game must not be fetched, uploaded, redistributed or committed; no game title/contents are required.**
3. A new, **original MIT, rights-cleared bootable or DOS `.COM` probe** should reproduce the exact `AH=1Bh` unsupported failure on the previous emulator and then, after the implementation, exercise **the entire related group** with known expected register, BIOS-work-area, GDC, port and framebuffer results. A probe must execute real guest x86 instructions on the actual CPU/firmware path; a mocked host BIOS reply is not sufficient.

## Implementation pointers

- [`src/firmware.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/firmware.rs): `execute_service` `0x18` branch currently implements `AH=0Ah–0Eh,10h–14h,16h–18h,1Ah,40h–42h,4Ah` but not the requested `0Fh,1Bh–1Eh`.
- [`src/bus.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/bus.rs): `0x68` already recognizes KCG mode codes `0Ah/0Bh` (Ap), while `Bus.cg_dot`, `text_enabled`, `Gdc` pitch/start/cursor and renderer use partly independent state. Ensure BIOS calls and direct I/O stay consistent, with actual display effects and no reset-induced desynchronization.
- [`src/gdc.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/gdc.rs), [`src/font.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/font.rs) and graphics/text VRAM mapping: reuse original device model rather than creating BIOS-only phantom state. The existing renderer addresses a fixed 80-column text grid; test and implement the meaningful supported variations.
- [`docs/hardware.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/hardware.md#boot-firmware) and [`docs/dos-compatibility.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/dos-compatibility.md): document the implemented subset and real remaining limitations.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Create a **small contract matrix** for `AH=0Fh,1Bh,1Ch,1Dh,1Eh` (and relevant existing neighbors): supported profile, documented inputs, outputs, preserved registers/flags, BIOS work-area impact, device/renderer effect, reset state, and explicitly unsupported variants. Resolve ambiguity from original NEC material, not emulation-code guesses.
- [ ] Add original, reproducible **red-before/green-after** guest tests for the reported `AH=1Bh` and the **other four missing services**, at least one realistic combined sequence (CRT initialization → KCG access mode → display area/width → cursor configuration → restore). Assert actual GDC/port/text VRAM/framebuffer behavior and preserved registers—not only absence of an exception. Where blink/timing matters, use deterministic bounded guest ticks/render frames.
- [ ] Test **code/dot KCG mode** both via BIOS and direct port `68h`, including CG ROM/user-defined characters and reversible switching. Verify that the text/Kanji restrictions and reads behave according to the documented profile, rather than incorrectly switching graphics resolution or destroying character RAM.
- [ ] Test display-area, width, cursor position/shape/visibility/blink and relevant mode-set/sense round trips. Confirm that shared state is coherent across BIOS, hardware I/O, firmware initialization, screen updates and CPU reset; reject documented invalid requests correctly without corrupting previously set state.
- [ ] Preserve existing guest FreeDOS(98) **`DOS=HIGH` / HimemX**, the 605 KiB (619,664-byte) conventional-memory probe, HDD boot/writes/export, FDD hot swap, VM profile and existing text/font/video/CG/graphics regressions. The additional CRT feature must not require a proprietary BIOS, font or game.
- [ ] Run native Rust/unit/guest tests and production **release-Wasm Chromium** against the same original guest probe at both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, with cold boot and reset where the behavior differs. Assert actual screen pixels/text or relevant hardware state, error-free execution and original disk bytes. Keep generated fixtures out of public Pages and preserve the strict published-asset audit.
- [ ] Run applicable documented fixture/source/license prep, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, real release-Wasm build and the full appropriate Chromium suite. Apply [the test/CI performance principles](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md#test-and-ci-performance-principles); report specific test results and failures.
- [ ] Author English PR/review/commit messages and original implementation code only; do not copy/translate existing emulator code, use NEC ROM dumps, insert game-specific bypasses, or require a user/private-image/manual/deployed-site check before merging.

## Optional validation

After merge, the user may privately re-run their lawfully held game to see if it progresses beyond `INT 18h/AH=1Bh`. A later unsupported service is a separate diagnostic, **not a reason to force the user to disclose copyrighted game data**. The maintainer may decide whether another cohesive display-BIOS family should be scheduled based on independent observed evidence.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
